newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht hits 14-year high offshore late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht hits 14-year high offshore late.

text.p: The Thai baht jumped to a 14-year high against the dollar in late trade offshore on strong demand and rising short-term baht interest rates abroad, dealers said.
The baht rallied to 22.800/23.000 late from 23.050/23.150 in the afternoon and 23.460/23.560 in the early morning, dealers said.
Dealers said baht liquidity was very tight in the offshore market due to the maturity of several one-month forward contracts since the baht attack in the middle of May.
They added costly tom/next and swap premiums to an equivalent interest rate of about 300 percent today also prompted people to offload dollars for baht in the spot market.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was traded at 150/180 satangs per dollar late compared with 200/260 in the afternoon and 165/185 in early morning.
The Bank of Thailand has imposed strict measures to cut off baht supply to offshore parties since the last speculative attack on the baht in the middle of May.
Since then, offshore players have faced a shortage of baht to cover their short positions taken during the attack, dealers said.
In the domestic market, the baht was weaker to 25.820/25.840 late from 25.800/25.810 early on strong commercial demand for dollar here, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 12.75-13.00 percent late from 13.00-14.00 in the afternoon.
